cim: Practical workshops on Artificial Intelligence Applied to Legal Research begin today
cim_eredeti: Practical workshops on Artificial Intelligence Applied to Legal Research begin today
szoveg_eredeti:
The Regulation Research Group launches a series of practical workshops on artificial intelligence applied to legal research, taught by Andrés Marzal (Universitat Jaume I)

Today, 9 November, marks the beginning of the Practical Workshops on Artificial Intelligence Applied to Legal Research, organised by the Regulation Research Group at the University of Valencia and taught by Andrés Marzal Varó (Universitat Jaume I).

The programme will take place on 9, 16 and 23 November 2026, with a final session on 14 December 2026, from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.In-person sessions will be held in Room 3P12 of Administrative Law at the Faculty of Law of the University of Valencia, with the possibility of online attendance via https://aulavirtual.uv.es/mod/url/view.php?id=3948537.

Artificial intelligence is already becoming part of the work of anyone conducting legal research, and its importance is likely to increase in the short and medium term. The course consists of four highly practical sessions, with participants working directly on their laptops to learn how to apply AI tools rigorously to the tasks involved in legal research.

The theoretical component is limited to building a conceptual framework that helps participants understand what happens when using generative AI: how these systems learn, why they are not deterministic, what hallucinations are and how their effects can be mitigated, what an AI agent is, and how AI systems interact with external sources such as the internet, databases and personal documents.

The aim of the workshops is to learn how to systematise the efficient resolution of common research tasks and to verify the outputs generated by AI systems. To achieve this, participants will work on activities that form part of everyday academic research, including searching, summarising, discussing, organising, connecting, analysing, comparing, verifying and arguing.

The approach is entirely practical. Each session concludes with a tangible output that remains useful after the course ends. Participants will leave with a configured AI assistant for research purposes, a workflow for producing case-law summaries, an AI-assisted thematic research wiki, and tools for monitoring developments related to their research topics.

To participate fully in the workshops, attendees are required to have an active Claude Pro subscription during November. The subscription currently costs approximately €20 for one month, according to current pricing, and is separate from the course itself, which is offered free of charge. Participants may cancel the subscription once the training period has ended.
